clue.text: Epiphany came as our smallest denomination financially declined

blocks.note: first meaning: an idiom for finally understanding something
second meaning, read literally: the penny, Britain's lowest-value coin, fell in value

explanation.surface: A sudden insight arrives just as the humble penny loses its worth.
explanation.walkthrough: The penny is the smallest British coin; read literally, the phrase describes it falling in value. The puzzle's theme is falling and gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the moment someone at last grasps a point, which is exactly what an epiphany is.

clue.text: Totally how to enter answer for this clue and the one before

definitions.text: how to enter answer for this clue and the one before

blocks.note: first meaning: thoroughly, completely

blocks.clueFragment: how to enter answer for this clue and the one before
blocks.note: second meaning: both this and the previous clue are downs, written in the grid starting at the top cell

explanation.surface: An instruction on how to fill in two consecutive answers.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks about its own position: this entry and 1 Down both run vertically in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning thoroughly or entirely, as in searching a house end to end.

clue.text: I'd connect somehow with another one falling at the same time

indicators.note: somehow suggests things are put together in some unspecified way, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
one is I, the Roman numeral, and another one adds a second

explanation.surface: Someone claims they'll link two things that happened to occur together.
explanation.walkthrough: The first phrase supplies one I already; another one adds the second I the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that happen simultaneously are coincident, so falling at the same time describes them.

clue.text: Indulge in free fall as part of risky diversion

indicators.note: as part of tells us the answer sits inside the following words, letters running across them

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone takes up free-fall jumping as a dangerous pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping from a plane and falling before opening a parachute is free fall, the essence of this sport.

clue.text: Performer at the top or scoundrels rising to it

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

blocks.note: rats are contemptible, treacherous people

explanation.surface: A headliner reached the top, or perhaps villains clambered up there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to the top, so the scoundrels rise to the top of the column, reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is the leading performer, the one billed at the top.

clue.text: How one's brought back to earth in field

definitions.text: How one's brought back to earth in field

blocks.clueFragment: How one's brought back to earth
blocks.note: surface reading: how a dreamer is made to face reality again
setter's reading: literally pulled down to the planet by a force field, the physics of falling

explanation.surface: Someone with lofty ideas is brought down to earth in their area of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' looks like a sphere of expertise; it is the physicist's field of force pulling objects to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects are pulled to earth by the planet's gravitational attraction, so the adverb tells how that happens.

clue.text: Completely prone to face this way?

blocks.note: first meaning: an idiom for thoroughly, as in 'that suits me'
second meaning: someone lying prone faces the earth beneath

explanation.surface: Someone is wholly inclined to look in a certain direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone' looks like 'inclined to'; it means lying face downward, so one faces the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning entirely or perfectly, as in something suiting one exactly.

clue.text: Doctor John was his assistant for many cases

definitions.text: Doctor John was his assistant for many cases

blocks.note: surface reading: a physician named John helping a colleague in medical cases
setter's reading: Dr John Watson helped a famous fictional detective solve crimes

explanation.surface: A doctor called John helped someone with a large caseload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' suggests patients; they are criminal investigations in Conan Doyle's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr John Watson is the companion and chronicler of Conan Doyle's great consulting detective.

clue.text: Serious fear leader in Times has something wrong with it

indicators.note: the leader is whatever comes first, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of the newspaper's name
an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A frightening editorial in the Times newspaper contains a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a newspaper editorial; here it simply means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme or intense fright, a stronger synonym for fear.

clue.text: Going back, identify old man as one of our ancestors

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: to name someone is to identify them
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Tracing a family tree, someone identifies an elderly man as a forebear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is slang for father, not an elderly man.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape-man is a primitive hominid, imagined as a distant evolutionary forebear of humans.

clue.text: Getting behind wheel with added energy

indicators.note: with added means something extra is slipped into the word, here inside it

blocks.note: being behind the wheel of a car means driving it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone is getting behind the wheel with renewed vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' seems to start a phrase about taking the wheel; it is the definition by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive something is to obtain it from a source, so deriving is a synonym of getting.

clue.text: Overturn function of multinational organization

blocks.note: the United Nations
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: Someone reverses a role belonging to an international body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a role or purpose; it is a social event, a do.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a decision is to reverse or cancel it, which is to overturn it.

clue.text: Warrant for admission is missing from home inspection

indicators.note: missing from says the preceding word is absent from what follows, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: being in means being at home
taken as written
an official visitation is an inspection

explanation.surface: A search warrant is absent from a home inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the second and third letters from the inspection word and put IN before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An invitation is what entitles a guest to entry, a sort of permit to be admitted.

clue.text: Has a wee dram, replaces ball on course

blocks.note: first meaning: drinks a small amount of whisky
second meaning: in golf, a player drops a ball to put it back into play after a penalty

explanation.surface: A golfer has a nip of whisky and puts a new ball down on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, a player whose ball is unplayable or lost may drop a ball from shoulder height, called taking a drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop is a small drink, and in golf a ball released by hand after a penalty is also a drop.

clue.text: Garden shrubs – or try elms for a change

indicators.note: for a change suggests making something different, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: plant these bushes, or elm trees if you want something different.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen flowering bush often grown in gardens.

clue.text: Do some artwork – in the blue, lacking detail

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one word goes within another

blocks.note: etching is a form of artwork made by engraving a plate
the blue is a poetic phrase for the sky

explanation.surface: Painting a picture while feeling sad leaves it vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do some artwork' tempts one to write SKETCH; it is ETCH, placed inside the blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketchy account is rough and incomplete, given only in outline.

clue.text: Inside story appropriately placed, doubly so

blocks.note: first meaning: the confidential facts about something
second meaning: both halves of the answer mean beneath, fitting for an entry that sits low and runs vertically

explanation.surface: The private details are positioned just right, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry runs vertically near the bottom of the grid, so it is placed twice over in keeping with the two words that make it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal slang for the real, private information about something.

clue.text: Testing periods as result of strange absorption

indicators.note: strange means odd or unfamiliar, telling us the letters appear in a peculiar new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Trial spells arise from some odd kind of taking in.
explanation.definitionFit: A probation is a trial period in which a new employee or offender is assessed.

clue.text: Start of spectrum initially rearranged for rave-up

indicators.note: initially means at first, so each colour named contributes only its opening letter
rearranged means put in a different order, so the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: the spectrum begins red, orange, yellow, green

explanation.surface: The beginning of a rainbow is shuffled to make a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: The rainbow's colours in order are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet; the first four supply their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild, unrestrained party, and a rave-up is British slang for a lively party.

clue.text: Unable to face house or pad guest trashed

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone can't face going home, or a visitor wrecked their flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is the theatre audience; an actor upstaged by a colleague further back must turn away from the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstaged actor is forced to turn their back to the audience, so cannot face the house.

clue.text: Outfit starts off game at rock bottom

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so each following word gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: opening letter
opening letter
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: A sports team begins a match at the foot of the league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' looks like a team; it means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, especially distinctive dress, which is what an outfit is.

clue.text: Be tediously persistent as battleaxe

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: to continue for too long
second meaning: a fierce, domineering woman

explanation.surface: A formidable woman goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer is a phrasal verb; as one word it is a fearsome person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a dragon and a battleaxe are slang for an aggressive, intimidating woman; dragging on is going on wearyingly.

clue.text: Artist in relation to one of his colours

blocks.note: re means concerning or regarding
noir is French for black, one of a French painter's colours

explanation.surface: A painter is linked to a shade he often used.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for black is in French because the painter was French.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a leading French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Mistakenly download – it might contain old chestnuts

indicators.note: mistakenly means done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An accidental download might be full of stale, overused jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old chestnuts' are tired jokes in the surface; in the definition they are aged chestnut trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut trees grow in forests, so a wooded area might include old ones.
